mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let’s bring all of this together. We’ve seen that the harm of coming into existence is very real—something we can’t avoid, and honestly, something we don’t talk about enough. Consent just isn’t possible when it comes to creating life, and that makes the choice to bring someone into the world a lot more complicated than we usually admit. And it’s not just about humans—every sentient being faces risks the moment they’re born. No matter how much social pressure we feel, or how strong our traditions are, those things just can’t justify exposing someone to harm, can they? Creating a life is something you can’t take back, and it’s a decision that echoes for a lifetime. But here’s what this really means for you. These ideas aren’t here to leave you feeling hopeless or stuck. Instead, they’re an invitation to see life, and the act of creation, with fresh perspective. The questions we’ve explored aren’t easy, and maybe they never will be. Still, when we face the reality of harm, we open the door to more compassion, more honesty, and a deeper way of living. Whether you decide to have children or not, whether you lean on tradition or feel ready to challenge it—the most important thing is to act with care. Care for yourself, for others, and for this world we all share. It’s not about saying no to life—it’s about really honoring just how much our choices matter, and the lives they touch. In a world that’s always uncertain, the courage to question, to reflect, and to act with kindness—that’s something truly powerful. So, take these insights with you, and let them inspire the way you move forward.
